title: Brown's work in the B-2 and Floyd Odlum's funding

tellings.quote: In fact, Floyd Odlam, who is the majority owner of Northrup, who funded Brown's work in the 60s, paid Brown 4,000 bucks or I don't remember, 2,000 bucks 4,000 bucks a month, his family uh uh the same amount uh until until he died.

plain: Michels says that Floyd Odlum, whom he calls the majority owner of the aircraft maker Northrop, funded the inventor Thomas Townsend Brown's work in the 1960s and paid him 2,000 or 4,000 dollars a month (Michels can't remember which), then kept paying Brown's family the same until Odlum died. Michels tells this himself without naming a source. He ties it to the idea that Brown's ideas found their way into the B-2, the stealth bomber Northrop later built, which would mean a major aircraft company quietly backed this fringe research for decades.
